children: ServiceTitan
shares tanked nearly 20% during early trading on Wednesday following the second-quarter earnings
by the software platform for the trades industry.

Although financial analysts labeled the results as "underwhelming," they identified a future growth driver through ServiceTitan Max, an AI-powered, end-to-end operating system designed for residential service and replacement businesses.

"We blame the weakness on idiosyncratic HVAC demand driving usage revenue below expectations and a new AI strategy," said Needham analyst Scott Berg in a Wednesday investor note. "TTAN is heavily pushing Max towards both new and existing customers given early indicators of Max's capabilities driving much higher demand. While this unlocks a major ASP uplift in the medium term, the new focus will de-emphasize non-core R&D even excluding the planned delay of new verticals. That said, we think TTAN can still sustain 20% platform growth while investing heavily in a long-term opportunity and weathering accounting-based rev rec headwinds."
Needham retained its Buy rating and $100 price target on the stock.
Similarly, Wells Fargo maintained its Overweight rating but reduced its target to $105 from $115.

"After a consistent set of quarterly results, FQ2 unlocked a series of bigger changes (greater Max prioritization & related impacts, more modest GTV growth assumptions, etc.), which we agree w/ LT but expect will pressure shares NT," said Wells Fargo analyst Michael Turrin in a note.
Meanwhile, Morgan Stanley kept its Overweight rating but lowered its price target to $92 from $124 and removed ServiceTitan from its "top pick" listing.

"ServiceTitan exceeded their goal of doubling Max locations in Q2 and now expect to end FY27 with over 700 locations, but because Max requires such substantial change management, ServiceTitan does not typically bill customers for the first quarter of a contract before ramping to full contract value by the end of the first year," said Morgan Stanley analyst Chris Quintero in a note.

"Furthermore, management decided to pause their expansion into new trades to allow them to execute on the Max opportunity within existing trades first," he added. "The impact of these two dynamics is that there are now a higher proportion of new deals coming from Max, leading to this timing lag in revenue recognition, which management expects to be between a $2-$3 million subscription revenue headwind over the rest of FY27."
In addition, ServiceTitan has decided not to charge existing customers an onboarding fee for transitioning to Max.
During Tuesday night's

, ServiceTitan CEO and co-founder Ara Mahdessian highlighted an example of how Max is working for one of its clients, Delponte Plumbing and Heating. Deplonte's president, Stacy Anapol, first implemented ServiceTitan in 2023 and became one of the first to use Max through a pilot program.

"Stacy's revenue grew more than 35% year-over-year during Q1 2026 and more than 45% year-over-year in the second quarter of 2026, accelerating as the quarter went on," Mahdessian said. "With Max, Delponte generated more calls, booked more appointments, and closed more sales with higher average tickets."

"But what impressed me most wasn't the revenue growth," he added. "It was what the operating model allowed them to do next. Delponte launched a new vertical entirely around recurring service. In just 3 months, they've already served 400 customers, all without adding a single back-office employee. Delponte's technician-to-admin ratio improved from 2:1 in 2025 to 3:1 in 2026, materially improving profitability."
ServiceTitan competitor Procore Technologies
was down 0.3% during pre-market trading on Wednesday. Salesforce
and SAP
were up 0.3% and 2%, respectively.
